title: Implicit Type Conversions
learning_outcomes: Explain the main idea behind implicit type conversions in your own words.
Apply implicit type conversions to a minimal C example and predict the result.
Identify a relevant boundary, portability assumption, or failure mode.

content.intro: This lesson explores Implicit Type Conversions through an original visual, a compact C example and a check you can perform locally.
content.why_it_matters: Understanding implicit type conversions helps you reason about C programs rather than relying on trial and error. It also helps you communicate assumptions, write safer code, and debug behavior across toolchains.

content_blocks.title: Core idea
content_blocks.text:
Implicit Type Conversions is studied as part of **Operators, Expressions, and Type Conversions**. Start with the contract: identify the inputs or program state, the rule C applies, and the observable result. Then check the behavior in a small, repeatable example.

The source curriculum also lists: Integer promotions, Usual arithmetic conversions, Signed and unsigned conversions. Keep these subtopics connected to the parent concept rather than treating them as unrelated trivia.

In C, details can depend on the selected language standard and implementation. Distinguish defined behavior from unspecified, implementation-defined, or undefined behavior, and consult the cited standard/compiler references when portability matters.

content_blocks.title: Practical reasoning
content_blocks.text: For “Implicit Type Conversions”, write down the preconditions first. Identify valid inputs and boundaries, decide which C rule applies, then choose evidence that would falsify your assumption. Prefer a small test with a clear expected result and compile with diagnostics enabled.

content_blocks.reset_steps: Restore the original example, rebuild with the same compiler flags, rerun the same inputs, and compare actual output with the stated result. For time-, platform-, or input-dependent examples, record the environment and do not expect identical values everywhere.
content_blocks.limitations: The CodeLeaf lesson page does not run C code. Compile locally or use a separately deployed, isolated C runner; do not execute arbitrary learner code inside FastAPI.

content_blocks.title: Portability and safety check
content_blocks.text: Use a documented standard mode; treat compiler extensions as extensions, not ISO C guarantees. Check return values, buffer bounds, and object lifetime. This course example is draft material and needs code review on the target toolchain before publication.

task: In a scratch file, create one small example that demonstrates implicit type conversions. Explain the expected result before running it, compile with warnings enabled, and record one boundary case or portability question.
hints: Reduce the program to the smallest example that still shows the concept.
Write down the input, expected result, and assumptions before running it.
Check the official language/compiler reference and test a boundary case.
expected_output: A short, reproducible C example and explanation showing implicit type conversions, plus a note about one boundary or portability consideration.
common_mistakes: Treating implicit type conversions as a rule to memorize rather than a behavior to test.
Ignoring compiler warnings, input validity, or object lifetime.
Assuming behavior observed on one compiler is guaranteed by every C implementation.
